script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 31. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
When wolves returned to Yellowstone, the rivers changed course.  How?  Wolves reduced deer populations.

Energy flows through ecosystems in food webs—plants capture sunlight, herbivores eat plants, predators eat herbivores. Each level depends on the level below. Remove one level and everything above it collapses. Some species have outsized effects—keystone species.  Wolves, sea otters, bees: remove them and ecosystems transform dramatically.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Nothing exists in isolation.  Ecosystems teach that everything connects to something else.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Connection Mapping - See Your Web.

Here's your activity: Map your own 'ecosystem'—what do you depend on? Food from farmers, electricity from power plants, ideas from teachers. Draw your web of dependencies. Like ecosystems, you're connected to more than you realize. This helps you recognize personal connections and dependencies.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how nature connects can be applied to connection mapping - see your web. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
